item.title: Russia Likely Used North Korean Missile In Deadly Ukraine Strike: Report
item.description: A Russian overnight attack that killed a family near the Ukrainian city of Kryvyi Rih likely used a North Korean missile, two sources said, in what would be the first time such a weapon had been fired in the war in nearly a year. Russia Likely Used North Korean Missile In Deadly Ukraine Strike: Report.

item.description: Analysis of samples collected from carcasses found traces of toxic chemical compound, says Kenya Wildlife ServiceThe recent deaths of 15 elephants near a park in southern Kenya in the past month were likely caused by the animals ingesting pesticides used on nearby tomato farms, the Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) has said. item.title: Japan’s earthquakes: Maps and graphics
item.description: A magnitude-6.8 earthquake struck in Japan near Kumamoto in Japan on July 28, one of the more powerful earthquakes this year recorded in the region. Here are graphics explaining the quake’s intensity, regional seismicity and more. Japan’s earthquakes: Maps and graphics.

item.title: Russia Launches Massive Missile And Drone Attack On Ukraine
item.description: Russia launched dozens of ballistic and cruise missiles, along with hundreds of drones, at Ukraine in the early hours of July 30 in another large-scale attack. Damage was reported in several cities, including Kyiv and Lviv. Russia Launches Massive Missile And Drone Attack On Ukraine.

item.title: US Military Says Latest Strikes Target Iran's Revolutionary Guards Corps
item.description: The US military said it launched dozens of strikes against targets linked to Iran's powerful Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) in response to Iranian attacks on American troops in Jordan after President Donald Trump had vowed to retaliate and "hit them very hard." US Military Says Latest Strikes Target Iran's Revolutionary Guards Corps.

item.title: Kyiv’s clear message to New Delhi: Not a single Ukrainian drone sent to Pakistan
item.description: This assertion becomes particularly important, especially in light of reports during Operation Sindoor alleging that Pakistani forces were being supplied with drones originating from Ukraine. This claim has circulated but remained difficult to independently verify Kyiv’s clear message to New Delhi: Not a single Ukrainian drone sent to Pakistan.

item.title: From Pajero culture to street protests: The struggle for accountability in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir
item.description: For decades, the Pakistani state has diplomatically showcased PoK to the world as if it were a separate country, complete with its own constitution, a Prime Minister as chief executive, and a President as constitutional head From Pajero culture to street protests: The struggle for accountability in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.

item.title: Ballots without a country: a quiet case for pluralism in Myanmar
item.description: In a country where geography mirrors diversity and authority remains contested, elections in Myanmar unfold detached from realities on the ground; with key Opposition forces excluded and large swathes of the nation outside effective participation, the exercise underscores how the absence of pluralism and federal accommodation continue to undermine any meaningful democratic transition Ballots without a country: a quiet case for pluralism in Myanmar.

item.title: Putin's Shifting Rhetoric Now Echoes Criticism He Once Aimed At Kyiv
item.description: In 2018, Russian President Vladimir Putin accused Ukraine of using the war in its eastern Donbas region to cover up its alleged economic and social problems. In 2026, Putin has been blaming "external enemies" for Russia's issues, including its growing fuel crisis caused by Ukrainian drone attacks. Putin's Shifting Rhetoric Now Echoes Criticism He Once Aimed At Kyiv.

item.title: Russia Pounds Ukraine With Missiles, Killing At Least Eight, Including Children
item.description: A barrage of Russian missile and drone strikes pummeled Ukraine overnight, killing at least eight people and injuring dozens of others as President Zelenskyy returned from the United States, where he said President Trump had agreed to provide Ukraine with licenses for Patriot missiles. Russia Pounds Ukraine With Missiles, Killing At Least Eight, Including Children.

item.title: Why is the founder of Telegram on Russia’s wanted list
item.description: The international wanted notice against Pavel Durov comes after the FSB said that Telegram had failed to remove “numerous channels, chats, and bots” allegedly used by “Ukrainian intelligence agencies and terrorist and extremist organisations” to prepare and coordinate acts of “sabotage and terrorism, mass murder, and cyber fraud” in Russia. Why is the founder of Telegram on Russia’s wanted list.

Beijing’s position that Taiwan must submit to absorption by the People’s Republic of China, even by force if necessary, is insistent and uncompromising. item.title: Ukraine’s Newest Battlefields: Online Retailers, Gas Stations, Shadow Fleets
item.description: Why is Ukraine pounding the warehouses and logistics centers of the company known as Russia’s Amazon? For the same reason it’s trying to drive Russian car owners crazy by forcing them to wait in crazy long lines at fueling stations. Ukraine’s Newest Battlefields: Online Retailers, Gas Stations, Shadow Fleets.

item.title: Does Iran's Attack On Jordan Mark A Shift In Military Strategy?
item.description: In what appeared to be the first time Tehran initiated an attack against US targets since the war in the Persian Gulf began in late February, Iran fired ballistic missiles at American bases in Jordan late on July 28. Does Iran's Attack On Jordan Mark A Shift In Military Strategy?

item.title: Rohingya refugees, Bahá’ís in Iran, disarmament in the Central African Republic
item.description: Independent UN experts on Wednesday called for urgent action to support Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh after reports indicated two boats carrying more than 500 passengers may have capsized off the coast of Myanmar in mid-July. Rohingya refugees, Bahá’ís in Iran, disarmament in the Central African Republic.

item.title: Hunger hampers Ebola response as cases top 3,200 in DR Congo
item.description: The UN emergency food agency appealed for immediate funding on Wednesday, warning that deepening hunger is undermining the response to an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) that has now infected more than 3,200 people. Hunger hampers Ebola response as cases top 3,200 in DR Congo.

item.title: UN warns West Bank settler violence hits ‘all-time high’ as calls grow to end occupation
item.description: Violence in the occupied West Bank is worsening as the Israeli Government continues to approve new settlements, while settlers and Israeli security forces have “often” acted together to attack local Palestinian communities, the UN’s human rights office (OHCHR) warned on Wednesday. UN warns West Bank settler violence hits ‘all-time high’ as calls grow to end occupation'.
